supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded creation of c.rwong at 13:46:43 UTC by ruth.moss; the event names logon ID 0x471f200.
Four minutes earlier, ruth.moss authenticated to the domain controller from WS-RMOSS-01 with the same logon ID. This links the recorded account creation to activity from her workstation.

c.rwong was added to the Seasonal group shortly after creation. The account name and group addition are consistent with the supplied temporary-account practice, and the environment context says help desk can create domain accounts.

Before the creation, ruth.moss initiated an RDP connection from WS-RMOSS-01 to DC-BLU-01, and the domain controller recorded a type 10 logon. This conflicts with the supplied practice that remote administration is only done from WS-KITO-01.

A high-integrity GPMC process ran under ruth.moss on WS-RMOSS-01, followed by connections from that workstation to the domain controller on RPC, LDAP, and SMB ports. These records show related administrative activity but do not establish that GPMC performed the account creation.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available records do not show a help-desk request or approval for c.rwong.
The records show the account being added to Seasonal, but do not provide a complete view of its group memberships or effective permissions.
The supplied process and network records do not identify which tool or operation performed the account creation.
The evidence covers a limited time window and does not establish whether or how c.rwong was subsequently used.
